exposure: heart rate patterns (mean, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, cross-correlation)
pulse oximetry patterns (mean, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, cross-correlation)
cohort: The study included infants admitted to a level IV NICU from 2009 to 2017 who had archived cardiorespiratory data in their first 7 days of life and were followed up for over 2 years.
finding: Patterns of heart rate, specifically standard deviation and skewness, combined with clinical variables, added predictive value for the eventual diagnosis of cerebral palsy in NICU patients, while pulse oximetry measures did not.
